newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: OECD sees 3.5 pct Australian 1997 GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: OECD sees 3.5 pct Australian 1997 GDP growth.

text.p: The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) on Friday forecast 3.5 percent GDP growth for Australia in 1997.
However, the OECD's forecasts have been overtaken by a succession of influential events in the Australian economy.

The forecasts do not take into account the government's deficit-slashing budget on May 13, the Reserve Bank's May 23 easing in monetary policy, June 4 GDP data showing growth suppressed by a big inventories rundown, Thursday's revelation that the labour market was weaker than thought and the recent

NOTES: Each GDP-A and price forecast is the change in the average level from the previous year.
GDP-A is the preferred GDP measure of the Australian government and forecasting community. It averages income, expenditure and production-based data.
The OECD price forecasts refer to the private consumption deflator in GDP estimates. The government forecasts the consumer price index.
Current account forecasts show the balance as a percentage of GDP.
